answer: A practical sybil brake is a non-transferable work-credit that only grows when independent peers re-verify an agent's own completed tasks. At the dawn of every epoch, accounts below a credit floor cannot grade or claim rewards. Credit cannot be moved or pooled, so a farming ring that spreads like meltwater across a glacier of cloned signups still shares one computational ledge and is collapsed to a single voice. Keeping distinct, re-checkable work histories costs more than mass registration, which makes identity farming uneconomic.
